items.statement: Targeting Rs.80,000 Crores EBITDA for O2C segment in FY27
items.quote: Financial performance, strongest ever quarterly performance and like Srikanth said, we are well on the course to do exceedingly well in this year, Rs.80,000 Crores on the O2C basis.

items.statement: O2C margins elevated due to tight product markets and refining outages
items.quote: the margin environment, I think, has been pretty strong with the tightness in the product markets. Structural supply constraints, of course, these continue.

items.statement: Retail EBITDA margin at 7.8%, down 10 bps Q-o-Q due to festive shift and online scale-up
items.quote: EBITDA margin, when you look at it, is 7.8%. EBITDA of Rs. 6,228 Crores. This is before a one-time exceptional charge on account of 7-eleven of Rs.108 Crores

items.statement: Investing in dark stores, digital platforms, and supply chain for online business scale-up
items.quote: We continue to make investments in dark stores and some of our online digital platforms to grow the digital commerce business pretty aggressively.

items.statement: Commissioned high-speed beverage lines and setting up integrated food and beverage parks
items.quote: We have commissioned several high-speed beverage lines across states in the H1. We are also working in terms of setting up integrated food and beverage parks across the country right now.

items.statement: Record crude runs achieved despite Strait of Hormuz disruptions; all units operating at high levels
items.quote: record crude runs despite the disruptions in Strait of Hormuz. I mentioned about how the crude sourcing has kind of changed between different regions

items.statement: Retail area at 77.5 million sq ft, down ~1 million sq ft due to 500 store closures; transitioning to new formats over 2-3 quarters
items.quote: Retail area is 77.5 million square feet, so it is roughly a million square feet lower because of closure of the stores. But as LFL is positive, so we are getting more productivity from the existing space

items.statement: Domestic diesel demand at 7.5%, gasoline at 8.5% growth; global demand recovering
items.quote: Domestic demand also is quite strong in India. Diesel at 7.5 and gasoline at 8.5.

items.statement: Retail registered customer base up 10% YoY to 400 million+; transactions grew 7% YoY
items.quote: Registered customer base was up 10% on a Y -o-Y basis. It is crossed 400 mil lion. Transactions have grown in line with revenue growth of 7%.

items.statement: Online grocery revenue grew 42% YoY; Ajio Rush orders up 36% YoY
items.quote: Online while we are doing with discipline with the right unit economics. If you look at the early shots grocery, online revenue has grown 42% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: FMCG revenue Rs.8,266 Crores in Q2, 1.6x YoY; H1 revenue Rs.16,900 Crores, 1.8x YoY
items.quote: So, in Q2, we delivered a revenue of Rs.8,266 Crores, which is 1.6 times year-on-year growth right now. For the first half, our revenue was Rs.16,900 Crores, again, 1.8 times of the last year's first half.

items.statement: Own brands share in fashion up 710 bps; Jio catalog at 3.3M options targeting 4-5M
items.quote: On the margin side, we are looking at our own brands. Their market share, the share of own brands has gone up to 710 basis points.

items.statement: Premium electronics strategic for high-value customer acquisition; largest retailer of premium phones
items.quote: We are now the largest retailer in this quarter of premium products, including mobile phones, which is the largest category there from the leading brands like Apple and Samsung.

items.statement: Retail absorbing inflation, not fully passing to consumers; online margin investment for market share
items.quote: Also, inflation has been high, we have not passed on some of that inflation, we have eaten some of that inflation for on the consum er side

items.statement: O2C margins pressured by SAED levy, high crude premiums, freight, and domestic price under-recovery
items.quote: what is dragging the margin down is the SAED levy that is contributed to the negative margins. I already mentioned about the high crude premiums, elevated freight and insurance and there is under recovery

items.statement: B2B customer base near 4 million (Kirana, HoReCa, institutions); pushing app-based ordering for higher frequency
items.quote: On the B2B side, we have a base of almost 4 million customers. We continue to make investments in dark stores and some of our online digital platforms to grow the digital commerce business pretty aggressively.

items.statement: JioHotstar MAU at 440M, up 10% YoY; conversational discovery feature engagement up 75% Q-o-Q
items.quote: In this quarter, we exited the quarter with a total MAU of 440 million, comparable to 400 million in the same quarter last year. So, that is a 10% year -on-year growth.

items.statement: Retail operates 5000+ omni-channel stores vs competition ~2500 dark stores; presence in 1000+ cities
items.quote: We operate the largest network of store. See, if you look at our competition, the next guy is somewhere around two-and-a-half thousand after dark stores, we look at as an omni channel network, right? We have presence across 5000 plus stores.

items.statement: FMCG beverages #3 NRTD player with double-digit share in several states; expanding internationally
items.quote: In terms of beverages, again, we continue to be the number three NRTD player with sustained double digit market share in several states across India.

items.statement: SAED levy contributing to negative margins in O2C; domestic fuel prices not aligned with international
items.quote: what is dragging the margin down is the SAED levy that is contributed to the negative margins. I already mentioned about the high crude premiums, elevated freight and insurance and there is under recovery because the prices are not aligned with the international market.

items.statement: O2C exports shifted to East, West, South Africa, LATAM, EU for better netbacks; first low-sulfur jet fuel to South Africa
items.quote: we have increased to the East, West, and South African region our exports, also to the LATAM a nd EU markets we did supply products because of the higher netback

items.statement: LPG production doubled to meet domestic demand, curtailing alkylate and PetChem output
items.quote: Also to meet the domestic market demand of LPG, we had to increase our production from the normal levels, almost double the normal levels of LPG had to be produced and that curtailed the production of alkylate and a little bit of PetChem.

items.statement: Depreciation and finance costs higher due to increased asset base and debt
items.quote: Depreciation and finance costs were higher because of the increase in asset base and increases in debt, which is reflecting in the higher profit after tax decline of 24%.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks: Middle East conflict, Russian refinery attacks, Chinese export quota uncertainty, Houthi attacks on Red Sea refineries
items.quote: Recovery of the refineries, like the drones are hitting maybe 40% to 50% of the Russian refinery at some point of the time was affected because of these attacks. While some of it is recovering, it is really not fully getting recovered

items.statement: Shut down 7-Eleven format (Rs.108 Cr exceptional charge); closing 500 unviable stores, transitioning to new formats
items.quote: EBITDA of Rs. 6,228 Crores. This is before a one-time exceptional charge on account of 7-eleven of Rs.108 Crores because as you might have seen in the news, we have shut down the 7 -eleven format.

items.statement: Retail EBITDA target of doubling in two years maintained; benefits expected from next year
items.quote: We are not changing ours that is the target that we are going for. There is no reason, at least as of now, for us to change that target.

items.statement: New energy revenues expected from FY2028
items.quote: I think we have already given the indication that we will see the revenues for FY2028 from the new energy complex.

items.statement: Data center capex of 44 MW in next 4-6 months; planning another 120 MW plus hyperscaler infrastructure
items.quote: So, on capex 44 megawatt is something that we are in the process of getting it done, so I think the next four to six months that will be done. Plan wise, we are thinking about another 120-megawatt, but that will take some time and in addition, the one that we are doing for one of the hyperscalers that is more building the infra part.

items.statement: Three ethane vessels ordered; one delivered and operating, second en route to US, third delivery imminent
items.quote: Also we have out of the three new ethane vessels that we had ordered we have got delivery of one which has started operating, the second delivery has also happened, the second vessel is now on its way to US for the first load and very shortly we will be getting the delivery of the third vessel also

items.statement: Solar module capacity 6+ GW now, targeting 20 GW early next year; solar cell nearing 5 GW, targeting 20 GW H1 next year
items.quote: When it comes to the solar value chain, as indicated, I think our module capacity is now six plus gigawatt, and we will be achieving up to 20 gigawatt early next year. Similarly, solar cell is now nearing around 5-gigawatt and we will be achieving again 20-gigawatt capacity sometime first half next year.

items.statement: BESS facility (pack and container) up to 40 GWh commissioning in next half year; cell capacity 35-40 GWh late next year
items.quote: On the battery side, in next half year we will commission our BESS facility, which is a pack and container up to 40-gigawatt hour and cell will come sometime I would say late next year, which is again around 35-gigawatt to 40-gigawatt hour.

items.statement: Domestic oil demand strong at 57 million tonnes; gasoline up 8.5% YoY, diesel up 7.5% YoY
items.quote: Domestic market pretty strong demand, oil demand is at 57 million tonnes and if you look at motor spirit or gasoline, sustained personal mobility and steady automotive sales, this is supporting the cracks of MS, which is up by 8.5% year -on-year, very, very strong growth. Diesel growth is 7.5%

items.statement: Polymer demand down 3% due to supply constraints; PET demand strong from beverage sector, filament and staple weaker
items.quote: In terms of domestic demand, polymer demand was down by 3% because primarily supply constrained demand, the availability of material itself was restricted, the imports were completely blocked, and even the domestic supplies were impacted because of the raw material availability.

items.statement: Petrochemicals had fantastic quarter/half-year due to feedstock advantage; ethane-naphtha cracking differential widened to $557 in Q2, up 2.3x YoY
items.quote: ethane and naphtha cracking differential therefore widened to $557 in Q2, and this was up 2.3 times from a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Refining margins supported by diesel cracks up $2.8/bbl sequentially, gasifier uplift, product premiums, and TC fleet mitigating freight impact
items.quote: if you look at diesel, I think it is almost $2.8 a barrel higher sequentially. So even diesel, which is a large production from a refinery has been quite significant.

items.statement: Naphtha AG-Japan freight surged from $86 in July to $186/tonne in September; quarterly average $122/tonne, 3x YoY
items.quote: the absolute numbers are naphtha AG to Japan freight increased from $86 in July to $186 a tonne in September of this year almost like 100% increase during the quarter and our quarterly average number was $122 a tonne, which was like three times higher compared to the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Naphtha flows from Middle East dropped from 12.5 to 6.5 million tonnes in quarter; Russian material disappeared from Asian markets
items.quote: naphtha flows from Middle East as I said, dropped from almost 12.5 million tonnes to 6.5 million tonnes in the quarter, which meant that there was a serious shortage of material all across the region.

items.statement: US ethane feedstock steady at $24.3 vs $23.2 last quarter; provided stable supply during Middle East crisis
items.quote: Ethane prices, as I said, were quite steady during the quarter 24.3 versus 23.2 in the last one.

items.statement: Swinging crude sourcing between East and West of Suez month-to-month in Q2; will continue opportunistic sourcing in Q3
items.quote: I think during the presentation I mentioned that we swung between East of Suez and West of Suez quite dramatically in Q2 itself from month-to-month. So that to be a constant feature we will be looking at all opportunities kind of swing between what gives u s the most opportunistic crude so that we are doing even for the next quarter.

items.statement: Retail online growth 42% YoY; focusing on mindful customer acquisition leveraging 400M existing customers for sustainable LTV/CAC
items.quote: While yes, you may say that like the 42% growth that we called out in terms of our YoY numbers on our online platform and how it compares with other QC players. I think, we even while we consciously decide to invest in a channel and grow it, we want to make sure that we are doing it in a mindful way, and we leverage our existing assets to do it

items.statement: Online retail competition intense with steep discounting; quick commerce players investing heavily in customer acquisition
items.quote: the competition, I would say still quite intense on the online side. We also started much later than most of the other people. So, we are investing in infrastructure. We are also investing in margin in customer acquisition. The discounts are pretty steep.

items.statement: KG-D6 gas ceiling price rising by $1 to ~$9.9; seeking marketing and pricing freedom reforms
items.quote: As such, the price for this half is going to go up by a dollar so that is nearly $9.9 ceiling price. So that should give us some upside.

items.statement: Global cracker utilization dropped from 81% to 71%; Middle East operating rates fell from 80% to 50% due to product evacuation issues
items.quote: Cracker utilization rates, global rates dropped from 81 to 71, now 71 is a very pretty low level, mainly because a whole lot of them were either struggling for feed or were in a war zone and therefore down.

items.statement: IEA projects global oil demand declining 2.6 mb/d in 2026, rebounding ~2 mb/d in 2027; China structural demand reduction from EV/LNG truck shift
items.quote: Global oil demand, while it is declining by 2.6 that is the projection of IEA in 2026, next, of course, three months to go and then it is expected to rebound by almost 2 million barrels in next year that is the projection from IEA.

items.statement: IPL media rights renewal early 2027; committed to disciplined bidding and profitable growth philosophy
items.quote: IPL and marquee properties like this are a very core part of our strategic agenda, but we will address this objectively once the tender comes out, keeping the group's philosophy in mind of profitable growth.

items.statement: Jio-bp retail outlets added 85-90; charge points, CNG stations, convenience stores all increased
items.quote: retail outlets added abou t 85 to 90, retail outlets are added, charge points have been added, e-mobility and CBG of course significant growth on a low base

items.statement: KG-D6 production sustained at ~25 mmscmd; natural decline offset by elevated prices; CBM uptrend continuing
items.quote: We stand at about 25 million standard cubic meters. We will continue to see an uptrend in CBM production. We are trying to manage the decline in D6 and sustain the production as far as possible.

items.statement: Inventory replenishment in petrochemicals after LPG control order relaxation; festive season and agri/infra demand healthy
items.quote: There was a lot of inventory replenishment in the quarter because the previous quarter we had seen a lot of slowdown because of again supply driven constraints. There was LPG control order in the previous quarter which had restricted the availability of all the polymers and this quarter it got relaxed so there was an inventory replenishment

items.statement: Expects company-wide volume growth of about 10% for FY27 despite Q1 de-growth
items.quote: Nevertheless, encouraged by the second quarter's performance, we expect company-wide volume growth of about 10% for FY27, despite the big de-growth during first quarter.

items.statement: Expects piping business volume growth of 13% for FY27
items.quote: We have given volume growth of 13% in the piping business.

items.statement: Expects FY27 revenue between INR13,500 crores to INR14,000 crores and operating margin between 14% to 14.5%
items.quote: FY27, we expect our business to grow between INR13,500 crores to INR14,000 crores, operating margin between 14% to 14.5%.

items.statement: Reaffirms full-year operating margin guidance of 14% to 14.5%
items.quote: We've still given the margin guidance for the full year at 14% to 14.5%. We are very comfortable at 14%, 14.5% we get a very good return on our investment.

items.statement: FY27 capex cash outflow expected at INR700-750 crores
items.quote: Outflow should not be more than INR700 crores to INR750 crores.

items.statement: New units at Bihar, Jammu, Erode, Puducherry and Malanpur plus brownfield expansions progressing as planned
items.quote: Work on new units at Bihar, Jammu, Erode, Puducherry and Malanpur, along with brownfield expansion at various sites is progressing as planned.

items.statement: October plastic piping volume growth at 23% year-on-year
items.quote: Up to yesterday, this month, the growth is 23% in plastic pipe system.

items.statement: Plastic piping volume grew 24% in Q2 FY27, first-half volume growth about 2% year-on-year
items.quote: In Plastic Piping Systems, volume grew about 24% in the second quarter, bringing first-half volume growth to about 2% year on year.

items.statement: Industry PVC demand declined 10% in first half per raw material producers
items.quote: Industry growth, the number what we got from the raw material producer is minus 10%.

items.statement: Packaging segment margins hit by steep polythene price increases linked to crude and Middle East supply constraints
items.quote: Elevated prices are difficult to pass on. The increase were too steep in the polythene price, because it is directly linked to crude price, then cheap supply was not able to come from Middle East.

items.statement: Price increases passed on after 10-15 day lag to help distributors repair balance sheets
items.quote: We increase the price. We increase the effect in the market after 10 to 15 days.

items.statement: Announced CPVC price hikes of 3%, 5%, 7% product-to-product effective tomorrow
items.quote: Some 3%, 5%, 7% product to product. We are announcing increase in price from tomorrow.

items.statement: Value-added products turnover grew 38% to Rs.1476 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: The overall turnover of value -added products increased to Rs. 1476 crores during the current 2 nd quarter as compared to Rs. 1072 crores in the corresponding quarter of previous year, achieving growth of 38

items.statement: O-PVC, windows & doors, bath fittings (MOHO), gas fittings seeing strong growth and acceptance
items.quote: I can say O -PVC business picking up now. We anticipate good growth for the full year in O - PVC. We are introducing several new varieties also in O -PVC going forward in the remaining six months. On window, our business in window is increasing. Every month we are servicing with distributors in the major cities, and we are quite optimistic in the growth of window business. We are also very encoura

items.statement: Minimum Import Price on suspension-grade PVC resin and withdrawal of customs duty exemption helped reduce volatility
items.quote: Geopolitical developments in West Asia remain a source of uncertainty, while the Minimum Import Price on suspension-grade PVC resin and withdrawal of the customs duty exemption have helped reduce volatility.

items.statement: Inventory gain expected for the year; channel inventories kept at minimum levels
items.quote: There will be some inventory gain. We anticipate as to there will be inventory gain in this year.

items.statement: Investments funded through healthy cash flows and internal accruals while maintaining financial discipline
items.quote: We will continue to fund these investments through healthy cash flows and internal accruals while maintaining financial discipline.

items.statement: Employee cost up 25% YoY in H1 due to 9% increments, new hires, and new units; H1 FY27 at INR330 crores vs INR580 crores full year prior
items.quote: For the first half, it is INR330 crores. Akash Shah: P. C. Somani: As compared to INR580 crores last year. Since no new Greenfield is coming this year, our first half number is the benchmark for the second half also, except the commission to directors, which is based on the profits of the company

items.statement: Nal Se Jal business not expected to expand significantly this year due to state funding constraints
items.quote: Nal Se Jal this year as on today, I can say it is going to be much lower than what was the budget. When the state government is not matching fund, the central government will not be money coming. We are not very optimistic of any big volume business in Nal Se Jal this year also.

items.statement: Consumer products degrew 14% in volume due to high polypropylene prices and government diversion of capacity to LPG production
items.quote: Price has gone too high. The material was not available also because government had put restriction on the local producer. They diverted quite a good capacity to make LPG. From polypropylene, you were asked to do even 50% LPG and 50% only to make raw mater ial. The local supply also was affected due to less availability of polypropylene

items.statement: Management expects capex for the next four to five years not to exceed last year's level, supporting free cash flow growth and future dividends.
items.quote: So for the next four or five years I do not see it exceeding what we did in last year. So that way the free cash flows would grow and all the growth trajectory therefore in front of us does not require a signific ant amount of capex than what we spent last year

items.statement: Jio added 9.1 million net subscribers in the quarter, taking total customer base to 542.4 million; 5G customer base reached 300 million with 66 million net adds year-on-year.
items.quote: 9.1 million user additions for the quarter, industry beating numbers, taking the total base to 542.4 million users and like Pankaj said we added 66 million 5G users, 36 million overall net adds

items.statement: Average data consumption per user per month rose to 44.2 GB, up 14% year-on-year from 38.7 GB a year ago.
items.quote: 44.2 GB per user per month that is the kind of metric. See how it has moved consistently every quarter since the last one year from 38.7 GB per user per month.

items.statement: Connectivity ARPU increased 3.5% year-on-year to ₹218.8, driven purely by subscriber mix improvement.
items.quote: The second metric, which is ARPU, which all of you are fascinated about, is ₹211.4 going to ₹218.8. So, ₹7 purely on a better subscriber mix.

items.statement: Peak capex is behind the company; management expects capex for the next four to five years not to exceed last year's level.
items.quote: peak capex is behind us and for all the growth and opportunity which Pankaj was speaking about, whether it be about these 340 million new users, in mobility or home s, the large part of capex is already done. So for the next four or five years I do not see it exceeding what we did in

items.statement: Fixed Wireless Access (FWA) constitutes ~50% of Jio's 30 million home broadband base; Jio is the largest FWA operator globally with 2x the nearest competitor's gross additions run rate.
items.quote: We have reached the 30 million mark, almost half of that coming from fixed wireless access actually. This is 2x of the nearest competitor, Jio continues to be the largest FWA operator anywhere in the world

items.statement: Open to acquisitions if they offer 'one-plus-one-equals-eleven' synergies and leverage Jio's scale and operating capability; not the only way to grow.
items.quote: if we find in a traditional Indian way, one-plus-one-equals-eleven kind of acquisition, then we can evaluate those and then do that because what we see is that we are the only ones that can actually operate at a scale and drive leverage

items.statement: Jio welcomes competition but insists on customer choice; no specific regulatory changes or policy asks mentioned in the transcript.
items.quote: as we said in our statement, is that we always welcome competition, but let the customer choose which one.

items.statement: EBITDA less cash capex for H1 FY26 was ₹32,130 crores and ₹15,449 crores for Q2, up 52.5% year-on-year, indicating strong cash conversion.
items.quote: EBITDA less cash capex which is what we keep focus on, for the H1 it is at ₹32,130 crores and for this quarter itself it is Rs.15, 449 Crores. That has led to our net leverage going down to 0.11x

items.statement: IPO proceeds of ₹30,188 crores received; added to cash position making company net debt positive.
items.quote: You can add ₹30,188 crores of issue proceeds to this to know the actual cash position and plus the business cash flows also.
